name: strava

verification.follow_up: Ratify against one known public club id once a Strava connection exists (no test account 2026-07-21).

report_profiles._api_notes: GET /clubs/{id} per configured club id (competitor ids from per-project config + own club ids from discovery). Public clubs only; a private/absent id returns 404 and is skipped with an alert (never a fabricated zero). member_count/following_count are point-in-time snapshot LEVELS: one dated row per club (grain club_id x date).

Own clubs only (discovered via GET /athlete/clubs). Persists the same club snapshot as competitor_snapshot; the membership-gated feeds (GET /clubs/{id}/members, /admins, /activities) are ANONYMIZED (first name + last initial, no athlete id, no stable PK) and are exposed as on-demand reads, cataloged as planned -- NOT persisted in v1 (privacy-lean default; decision recorded in the story).

_error_map_note: Reference: Strava API 'Authentication' (developers.strava.com/docs/authentication) + the Fault schema of developers.strava.com/swagger/swagger.json. PAYLOAD SHAPE: Fault = { message, errors[]: {resource, field, code} } -- the code sits inside an errors ARRAY, which core.pull_errors._extract_provider_codes does not descend into, so connector._strava_error_payload() lifts the first entry's code to the top level and keeps message + the whole errors array as evidence (the square normalisation pattern; core keeps zero provider vocabulary, AD-2). WHAT THE KEY BUYS: Strava's documented response to a token whose grant no longer exists is exactly {"message":"Authorization Error","errors":[{"resource":"Athlete","field":"access_token","code":"invalid"}]} with HTTP 401, and its deauthorisation contract is explicit -- when access is revoked, EVERY access and refresh token the application holds for that athlete is invalidated at once. So '401:invalid' is auth_revoked, not auth_expired: no refresh can recover it and the athlete has to re-authorise. The 400 codes stay invalid_request (what the status already says) but are declared so the vocabulary is written down where the next reader looks. TWO CONNECTOR SHIMS RUN BEFORE classify_http_error and are NOT expressible here: (a) a 403 whose Fault code is 'exceeded' (or X-RateLimit-Usage at/over the limit) goes to the core.quota.RateLimitError breaker, since Strava historically answers 403 rather than 429 on some endpoints; (b) a 404 on the competitor_snapshot path is an EXPECTED non-fatal 'unreachable' outcome (private or absent public club) -- the club is skipped with a meta alert, never raised. A 404 on own_club_full stays connector._STATUS_OVERRIDES -> permission_denied. 429 raises core.quota.RateLimitError (breaker path, Retry-After honoured) and is never keyed here. ORIGINAL AI-114 NOTE (2026-08-01, kept for the record): the former key '404' -> permission_denied was keyed on the HTTP STATUS ALONE -- a real judgment (a club the athlete should belong to that answers 404 is an access problem, not a transient unknown) but not a provider refinement, and DEAD as written: the map was passed to classify_http_error, which only ever looks up '<status>:<code>', so a 404 was classified 'unclassified' and retried. It now lives, live and explicit, in connector._STATUS_OVERRIDES, AFTER the competitor_snapshot 404-skip shim that the caller applies first. VERIFIE le 2026-07-21 (https://developers.strava.com/swagger/swagger.json). Strava error body = Fault { message, errors[]:{resource, field, code} }. 'code' is a FREE-FORM string (invalid/required/exceeded/missing/not found), NOT a stable enum, so no '<status>:<code>' key is defensible without a live pass (AI-13): the pure-HTTP taxonomy in core.pull_errors already lands 401->auth_expired, 403->permission_denied, 400->invalid_request, 5xx->provider_transient. 429 raises core.quota.RateLimitError (breaker path, honor Retry-After). TWO connector shims applied BEFORE classify_http_error: (a) a 403 whose Fault errors[].code=='exceeded' (or X-RateLimit-Usage at/over limit) is routed to the breaker as a rate-limit, not permission_denied (Strava historically returns 403 for rate-limit on some endpoints); (b) a 404 on the competitor_snapshot path is an EXPECTED non-fatal 'unreachable' outcome (private/absent public club) -> the club is skipped + a meta alert emitted, NEVER raised. A 404 on own_club_full (a club the athlete should belong to) stays a real permission_denied.

account_topology._comment: Strava Clubs topology has a SINGLE level: the connected athlete's OWN clubs (GET /athlete/clubs -> SummaryClub[]). discover_accounts enumerates them. The reporting entity (selection_level) is the CLUB. Access-check = GET /clubs/{id} returns 200 for a selected own club. COMPETITOR clubs are NOT in this topology: Strava exposes no club search/list endpoint, so competitor ids are arbitrary PUBLIC ids the token can read but does not own -> they are supplied as per-project config (strava_competitor_club_ids), validated at pull time by GET /clubs/{id} (200 public / 404 unreachable). No *_CLUB_ID env var (doctrine): own selection + competitor list live in connection_ref / project config.

quota._rate_limit_note: VERIFIE le 2026-07-21 (https://developers.strava.com/docs/rate-limits/): default 100 reads / 15 min (900s), 1000 reads/day; overall 200/15min, 2000/day. 1 club snapshot = 1 read. Conservative budget = 100 points / 900s. Backstop: 429 (and 403 'exceeded') -> RateLimitError.
quota.cost_note: 1 read per club per snapshot. own_club_full adds 1 (/athlete/clubs) + paged /members + paged /activities + 1 /admins per own club. Serialize pulls per connection.

fields.description: Total number of club members at the snapshot moment. Non-additive point-in-time level (aggregation_rule=latest); the growth trend is derived downstream. THE key competitive metric.
Number of accounts the club follows, at the snapshot moment. Non-additive point-in-time level (aggregation_rule=latest).
Snapshot date (YYYY-MM-DD), stamped at extraction (Strava returns no date; the club object is a point-in-time snapshot). Time grain of the fact.
Strava club unique identifier (DetailedClub.id). The snapshot grain key.
Club city (free-form; not an ISO code, renamed club_* to avoid vocabulary collision).
Club country (free-form, NOT an ISO-3166 code; renamed club_country to avoid colliding with the vocabulary-governed 'country' dimension).
Whether the club is private. A private competitor club is unreachable to a non-member (404 -> skipped).
Stamped by the connector: true for an own club (from discovery), false for a config-supplied competitor club.

population.note: Only the clubs whose public ids were supplied are requested; Strava exposes no club search, so an unknown club stays unavailable rather than discovered.

_max_provider_backfill_days_note: No max_provider_backfill_days is declared: this provider's published reporting window has not been established as of 2026-08-17. The key is left absent rather than filled with an estimate -- an invented re-collection bound promises the operator a history the provider never committed to. Establishing it means reading the provider's own documentation and recording the URL here, as the modules that do declare one have done.
